explanations: luna: The source-section says a name is what makes a thing known; Allah teaches Adam الْأَسْمَاءَ كُلَّهَا. | terra: God teaches Adam all the names, joining الاسم to عَلَّم: naming is knowledge, exactly as the section says a name is what makes a thing knowable.

luna: This neighbor completes the naming scene: Adam is told to inform the angels of the names, making the taught names usable for recognition. | terra: Adam informs the angels of the names, completing 2:31: the taught names are publicly articulated so the things can be identified, and God contrasts this with the angels' limited knowledge.
luna: The source-section says a name is raised and remembered; this verse condemns those who prevent Allah's name from being mentioned in His mosques.
terra: The worshippers are described by God's dye, صِبْغَةَ اللَّهِ. This is a specific parallel to the branded mark: a bestowed imprint identifies those devoted to its giver.

luna: The source-section dictionary form ع ل م is a distinguishing sign; Safa and Marwa are named as مِن شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ, visible ritual markers traversed in pilgrimage. | terra: Safa and Marwah are among God's شعائر, public sacred symbols. Their named, visible locations show how a place can function as a sign within worship.
luna: The source-section's opening joins Allah, الرحمن, and الرحيم; this verse names one God as Allah, the Most Merciful and Compassionate.
luna: The section calls creation a field of signs that can be known; this verse names the heavens, earth, rain, winds, ships, and clouds as آيَات for people who reason.
luna: The source-section marks an act with Allah's name; this verse excludes food over which another name was invoked.
luna: The section says a sign enables recognition; the new moons are appointed marks of time for people and pilgrimage.

luna: The source-section defines a sign as a mark by which something is known; the chest bearing relics is called آيَةَ مُلْكِهِ, the identifying sign of Saul's kingship. | terra: The return of the Ark is specified as the sign of Saul's kingship. A concrete object functions as the public mark by which an otherwise disputed claim is recognized.

luna: The source-section image is a mark by which a person is known; this verse says the needy are recognized by their سِيمَاهُم. | terra: The needy are known by their سِيمَا although they do not beg insistently; this gives the section's readable mark a quiet social form rather than a literal burn.
luna: The source-section defines a name as what identifies a person; Mary's mother says سَمَّيْتُهَا مَرْيَمَ, I have named her Mary.

luna: The source-section says the name raises and identifies the named; this verse names the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, then calls him وَجِيهًا in this life and the next. | terra: The angels announce a word from God whose name is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary. The stated name and title distinguish the announced person before his appearance.

luna: The source section defines an identifying sign; this verse says the Sacred House contains clear signs, including the standing place of Abraham, مَقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ. | terra: The Sacred House contains clear signs, including Abraham's standing place. A fixed place is named as a visible sign that identifies the sacred site and its history.

luna: The section says a mark distinguishes its bearer; this verse contrasts faces that turn white and faces that turn black on the Day of Judgment. | terra: On the Day when faces whiten and blacken, the blackened faces are addressed for disbelief. Visible color becomes a boundary-mark that makes contrary moral outcomes legible.
luna: This continuation gives the white-faced group its identity: they are in Allah's mercy and remain there.

luna: The source-section dictionary describes a rider with a mark in battle; here the angelic reinforcements are marked, مُسَوِّمِينَ, in a battle scene. | terra: The promised angels are مُسَوِّمِينَ, marked or bearing distinguishing marks in battle; it realizes the section's dictionary image of a rider's battle badge.
luna: This continuation calls the angelic support glad tidings and reassurance; it explains how the marked battle scene in 3:125 functions as a sign.

luna: The section treats creation as marks that disclose their maker; this verse calls the creation of heavens and earth and the night-day alternation signs for people of understanding. | terra: The creation of the heavens and earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for people of understanding; the world is explicitly presented as discernible indication.

luna: The section links signs with knowing and invoking the named Lord; these readers remember Allah and call him رَبَّنَا after reflecting on creation. | terra: Those who remember God read heaven and earth's creation as not purposeless. It gives the responsive act of understanding that completes the signs named in 3:190.
luna: The source-section treats a mark as identifying an animal's status; this verse forbids violating God's rites and specifically names offerings and garlands as a protected boundary.
luna: The source-section's بِسْمِ اللَّهِ marks an act under God; this verse forbids what was dedicated in the name of another.

luna: The source-section says a name marks the beginning of an act; trained hunting animals are sent with Allah's name mentioned over the catch. | terra: The hunter is told to mention God's name over what trained animals catch. An ordinary act is made answerable to the name, extending the beginning-under-the-name pattern.
luna: The source-section's branded camel is an animal marked for recognition; this verse groups sacrificial offerings with garlands, الْهَدْيَ وَالْقَلَائِدَ, as public institutions for people.

luna: The section's mark is for knowing; this verse makes stars landmarks for navigation and calls them signs for people who know. | terra: God makes stars for navigation in land and sea and details signs for people who know. Celestial markers perform the guiding function that 16:16 assigns to landmarks.

luna: The section says each kind of creation is a sign; this verse displays distinct crops, fruits, and growth as signs for people who believe. | terra: Rain brings forth plants, fruit, and their ripening, and the verse asks observers to look because these are signs. Observable growth becomes a readable display within creation.

luna: The source-section says naming identifies an act under Allah; this verse permits eating what has had Allah's name mentioned over it. | terra: Believers are told to eat what God's name has been mentioned over. The named act gives the source's opening formula a daily ritual form.
luna: This neighbor repeats the named-food rule while explaining its boundary and exception for necessity.

luna: The source-section puts an act under Allah's name; this verse draws the opposite boundary around food over which His name was not mentioned. | terra: Not eating what God's name was not mentioned over makes the boundary visible: an action without the name is described as defiance, reversing the marked act of 6:118.
luna: The section makes the name a sign that identifies allegiance; this verse condemns assigning rules to livestock whose meat was forbidden because Allah's name was not mentioned.
luna: The source-section places an act under Allah's name; this verse forbids an animal dedicated to someone other than Him.
luna: The source-section says an act begun under a name is placed under its bearer; this declaration dedicates prayer, sacrifice, life, and death to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

luna: The section links height to recognizable marks; people on الْأَعْرَاف identify both groups by their سِيمَاهُم. | terra: The people on the heights recognize every group by their سِيمَا; the verse stages precisely the identification by an outward distinguishing mark developed in the section.

luna: The section's marks identify people on the heights; this continuation has those on al-A'raf call men they recognize by their marks, يَعْرِفُونَهُم بِسِيمَاهُمْ. | terra: The people on the heights recognize particular men by their سِيمَا before addressing them, making the mark a basis for discernment and judgment.

luna: The source-section's name identifies what it names; Hud challenges his people over names they and their fathers assigned to gods without authority. | terra: Hud calls the objects of worship mere names his people and their fathers named, with no authority from God. These are the section's raised signs without a real referent beneath them.

luna: The source-section dictionary example is a branded camel; this verse calls Salih's she-camel an آيَة from Allah, a distinct camel-sign without saying it is branded. | terra: Salih calls the she-camel God's sign and commands his people to leave it to feed. A particular living creature is publicly set apart as a sign, not simply an animal.

luna: The source-section's names are identifying signs and calls; this verse says Allah has الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَىٰ and commands calling Him by them. | terra: God's most beautiful names are to be used in calling on Him. This directly extends the opening name from a label into an act of invocation.
luna: The source-section makes the invoked name a sign that places the listener before God; here believers' hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned.

luna: The section says signs enable knowledge; the sun, moon, and their measured phases let people know years and reckoning. | terra: The sun's radiance and the moon's measured phases let people know the count of years, and are detailed as signs for people who know. Celestial order serves recognition and knowledge.
terra: The succession of night and day and what God created in the heavens and earth are signs for the reverent. It extends the section's world-as-sign vision to recurring time.
terra: Pharaoh's body is preserved so that it may be a sign for those after him. A body left visible becomes an enduring identifying trace and warning.

luna: The source-section says an act begins under a recognized name; Noah calls the passengers aboard بِسْمِ اللَّهِ and places the ark's motion and stopping under it. | terra: Noah tells the passengers that the ark's course and mooring are بسم الله. The name is set over a concrete undertaking, as the section says an action is placed under the known sign.
luna: This neighbor continues the sailing scene named in 11:41, showing the ark moving among waves like mountains.
luna: The section names the ark's motion and mooring; after it sails in 11:41-42, this verse records it coming to rest on Judi, completing the stopping detail.

luna: The source-section dictionary form uses a camel bearing a mark; this verse likewise identifies Allah's she-camel as a sign and sets a boundary around its use. | terra: Salih calls the she-camel God's sign and tells his people to leave her on God's earth. It repeats the distinctive living-sign scene with its own command to preserve what identifies the message.
terra: The clay stones are مُسَوَّمَة, marked by their Lord for the transgressors; the same brand vocabulary becomes a precisely assigned punishment.
luna: The source section treats a trace as evidence; Joseph's brothers bring a shirt with false blood, بِدَمٍ كَذِبٍ, so the stain is a fabricated mark rather than a reliable sign.
luna: The source-section trace is something seen and read; Joseph's shirt is torn from behind, a physical clue whose meaning the following verses test.
luna: This continuation introduces a witness's front-versus-back test for the torn shirt; its contribution is the competing accounts that make the trace decisive.
luna: The source-section's trace-reading image meets the test of Joseph's torn shirt: its tear from behind, قُدَّ مِن دُبُرٍ, is the distinguishing evidence.
luna: This verse applies the garment test: seeing the tear from behind exposes the false accusation, so a physical trace separates truth from falsehood.

luna: The source-section word اسم is an identifying mark; Joseph says the gods people worship are only names, أَسْمَاء, that they and their fathers invented. | terra: Joseph says the objects worshipped are only names named by people and their fathers. The verse directly supplies the section's image of an elevated label unsupported by what it claims to identify.
luna: The section's dictionary gloss describes recognizing a trace in someone; Jacob says he senses Yusuf's scent, رِيحَ يُوسُفَ, as an identifying trace before the caravan arrives.
terra: Many signs in the heavens and earth are passed by while people turn away. It gives the section's whole creation-as-sign claim its opposite human response: failing to read what is visible.
luna: The section joins a raised sign to what is known; this verse says the raised heavens and subjected sun and moon are signs for certainty about meeting their Lord.
luna: The section presents each kind of creation as a marker; this verse distinguishes mountains, rivers, and gardens and calls them signs for people who reflect.
luna: The section says one kind of creation is distinguished from another; this verse contrasts neighboring plots and date palms watered by the same water as signs for people who reason.
luna: The source-section says a name is a raised sign and good mention spreads; this verse pictures a good word with firm roots and branches in the sky.
luna: The section's good-name image is a sign that remains; this verse reverses it with an evil word like a tree uprooted without stability.

luna: The section's trace-reading verse points back to a city turned upside down and pelted with stones; this ayah supplies the visible aftermath that 15:75 calls signs. | terra: The town is overturned and pelted with marked-like baked clay; this is the concrete ruined scene that 15:75 says the مُتَوَسِّمُون read, while 15:75 supplies the explicit reader.

luna: The source-section root و س م includes reading a trace; this verse calls the ruins آيَات for الْمُتَوَسِّمِينَ, those who discern marks. | terra: The section explicitly reads this as the Qur'anic counterpart to وسم: the ruined town contains signs for the مُتَوَسِّمِين, people able to read traces and marks.

luna: This continuation places the overturned town on a road that remains, making the aftermath in 15:74-75 a trace travelers can encounter. | terra: The destroyed place remains on an established road. Its location makes the aftermath in 15:74–75 available as a trace to be encountered and read.

luna: This continuation explicitly calls the same ruined town a sign for believers, completing the sign-reading scene introduced at 15:75. | terra: The aftermath of the town's destruction is again called a sign for believers. It confirms that the readable traces in 15:75 are not merely private inference but a disclosed sign.
luna: The section says the created world is made of signs; this verse calls the ordered night, day, sun, moon, and stars signs for people who reason.
luna: The section's الْعَالَمِين are created kinds, each a sign; this verse calls the varied colors of what is on earth a sign for people who heed.

luna: The source-section root ع ل م is explained as a distinguishing sign; this verse names عَلَامَات, landmarks by which a traveler can identify the way. | terra: Mountains, rivers, and routes are placed so people may be guided; 16:16 follows by naming landmarks and guiding stars. This ayah supplies the terrain and paths through which the next ayah's markers work.

luna: The section's sign is meant to guide recognition; this neighbor completes the landmarks with stars by which people find their way. | terra: God makes عَلَامَات, then stars by which people find their way. Raised landmarks and guiding signs give the section's flag-like علم a concrete Qur'anic scene.
luna: The section says created things are signs that disclose what they are not; after describing creation, this verse distinguishes the Creator from what does not create.
luna: The section treats each created kind as a sign; the bee's varied honey is called a sign for people who reflect.
luna: The source-section's named beginning marks allegiance; this verse excludes what has been dedicated to other than Allah.

luna: The section's sign makes something knowable; night and day are two signs used to count years and reckoning. | terra: Night and day are made two signs, with the day made seeing so people can seek bounty and know number and reckoning. Their contrast is designed to be read.
luna: The section uses an attached brand as an identifying mark; this verse pictures each person's deeds fastened to the neck and a record brought out on judgment day.
luna: The source-section dictionary example is a branded camel; this verse calls Thamud's she-camel a visible sign, الناقة مبصرة, without claiming it bears a brand.
luna: The section defines a name as what identifies its bearer; this verse calls each people with its imam, بِإِمَامِهِم, an indirect identifying affiliation rather than a literal name.

luna: The source-section says names identify and call their bearer; this verse permits calling Allah or الرحمن and says the beautiful names belong to Him. | terra: Call on Allah or call on al-Rahman: the verse joins the two names in the opening and says the most beautiful names belong to Him, so the name directs a real call.
luna: The source-section dictionary form أَثَر is a trace one reads; Moses and his companion follow their آثار to find the place they sought.

luna: The source-section dictionary form سَمِيّ appears here in its ordinary namesake sense for Yahya, distinct from the divine no-equal question at 19:65. | terra: Yahya is given a name for which God says He has made no prior سَمِيّ. The name distinguishes this promised child by denying an earlier namesake.
terra: God says that Jesus will be made a sign for people and a mercy. The promised child is therefore a living, publicly legible sign before the later world-sign formulations.

luna: The source-section gloss describes a good name raised among people; this verse gives Abraham's family لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ عَلِيًّا, an elevated truthful mention. | terra: God grants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob a lofty truthful mention. A high reputation gives the source's raised-name image a concrete Qur'anic form.
luna: The source-section describes a good name as raised mention; this verse commands, وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ إِدْرِيسَ, to mention Idris in the Book.
luna: The source-section links the name to height; after 19:56 tells readers to mention Idris in the Book, this verse says God raised him to a high station.

luna: This angelic reply says their descent is only by their Lord's command; that stance of acting under His authority sets up, but is distinct from, 19:65's worship and namesake question. | terra: The speakers say they descend only by the Lord's command; this supplies the immediate voice and command-context for 19:65's worship of the one without a namesake.

luna: The source-section dictionary form سَمِيّ means a counterpart deserving His name; this verse joins worship with the question whether He has any namesake or equal. | terra: After commanding worship and patience, the verse asks whether one knows for God a سَمِيّ. It makes the source's namesake sense a test of whether any equal can bear the divine name.

luna: The source-section discusses Allah's names as ways to call and know Him; this verse says the most beautiful names belong to Allah alone. | terra: Allah has no god but Him and possesses the most beautiful names. The verse anchors the section's claim that the greatest name is a name of the uniquely worshipped referent.
luna: The source-section places worship under the known name; here God identifies Himself as Allah, then commands worship and remembrance.
luna: The section reads created kinds as marks; this verse describes the earth's paths and the water that brings out distinct plants.
luna: The source-section says each created kind is a sign; this continuation points to diverse plants and livestock as signs for people of understanding.

luna: The section says each created kind can be a sign; Mary and her son are explicitly made آيَةً لِلْعَالَمِينَ. | terra: Mary and her son are made a sign for the worlds. A living human relation becomes an ayah addressed to all the created kinds named by عالمين.

luna: The source-section says an act can be marked by Allah's name; pilgrims are told to mention His name over the livestock He provided. | terra: Pilgrims are to mention God's name on appointed days over the livestock He provided. The name is spoken over a concrete provision and communal act.

luna: The source section describes a raised sign that is recognized and honored; this verse says honoring شَعَائِرَ اللَّهِ comes from piety of hearts. | terra: Honoring God's شعائر is linked to piety of hearts. The verse connects an outward sacred sign with the inward recognition to which it ought to lead.

luna: The source-section's name identifies the giver and consecrates an act; every community is told to mention Allah's name over its provision of livestock. | terra: Every community receives rites so it may mention God's name over the livestock He has provided. Naming frames sacrifice across communities, not just Noah's particular journey.
luna: The source section connects God's name with worship; between the rite in 22:34 and the named offerings in 22:36, this verse describes hearts trembling when Allah is mentioned.

luna: The source-section links God's name to an action on an animal; here Allah's name is mentioned over sacrificial camels standing in rows. | terra: The sacrificial camels are among God's شعائر, and His name is pronounced over them while standing. A visible ritual marker and the divine name converge in one act.
luna: The section treats the name as a sign that identifies an act; this verse sets the outward meat and blood apart from the piety that reaches Allah.
terra: Monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques are places in which God's name is much mentioned. The name is thus preserved and raised publicly in built spaces of worship.
terra: God has named the community Muslims before and in this revelation. A collective name here publicly identifies a people and their witness-bearing role.
luna: The section says each created kind is itself a marker; this verse makes livestock a عِبْرَة, pointing to their milk and other benefits as a concrete created kind to recognize.
luna: This verse gives the ark scene that frames Noah's later words of praise and prayer when aboard in 23:28-29.
luna: The source-section presents an action placed under God's name; Noah's passengers are told to praise Allah when settled aboard the ark.
luna: The source-section has Noah name God over the ark's course and landing; here he prays, رَبِّ أَنْزِلْنِي, for a blessed landing.
luna: This continuation interprets Noah's ark story from 23:27-29 as containing signs, إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ, linking the vessel scene to the section's world-as-sign image.

luna: The section joins a sign with height; Mary and her son are made آيَة and sheltered on رَبْوَةٍ, an elevated place. | terra: The son of Mary and his mother are made a sign and placed on an elevated, settled place with water. The verse joins a living sign to the section's imagery of height.

luna: The source-section links a name to elevation; this verse speaks of houses raised and Allah's name remembered within them. | terra: In houses God has permitted to be raised, His name is remembered. Physical elevation and the utterance of the name are joined in one worship scene.
luna: This neighbor shows the named houses in use: trade does not distract their people from remembrance, prayer, and giving.
luna: The section makes the created order readable; this verse calls the alternation of night and day a lesson for people with sight.

luna: The source section notes resistance to the name الرحمن; here people ask who الرحمن is when told to prostrate to Him. | terra: When told to prostrate to al-Rahman, they ask what al-Rahman is. Rejection of the name blocks the worship and recognition that the opening name invites.
luna: The source-section dictionary form الْعَالَمِينَ means the created world; Pharaoh asks who its Lord is, making the world's identity the question.
luna: The source-section dictionary gloss of الْعَالَمِينَ includes the heavens and what they contain; this answer defines the worlds as the Lord of the heavens, earth, and between them.

luna: The source-section says a good name travels among people; Abraham asks for لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ فِي الْآخِرِينَ, a truthful mention among later generations. | terra: Abraham asks for a truthful mention among later people. The request clarifies that a good name is a continuing recognizable trace after its bearer.
terra: The people of Aad build an ayah on every high place for play. A raised monument is called a sign, but its vain construction reverses the section's sign that leads to genuine recognition.

luna: The source-section's name at a letter's head identifies its sender; the queen first reports receiving a noble letter, setting up the identification in 27:30. | terra: The queen first identifies the object cast to her as a noble letter; 27:30 then gives its named header, so this verse supplies the recognitional setting for the opening formula.

luna: The source-section says بِسْمِ الله identifies whose name an act or message bears; this letter states it is from Solomon and begins in God's name. | terra: Solomon's letter begins with بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم. At the head of writing, the name identifies both the letter's source and the authority in whose name it speaks.
terra: The abandoned houses of the wrongdoing people are called a sign for people who know. Their visible desolation is a trace that can be read, like the ruined town in 15:75.
luna: The section's sign makes a thing perceptible; this verse contrasts night for rest with a day made visible and calls it signs for believers.
terra: God will show His signs and people will recognize them. The verse directly links displayed signs with recognition, the function the section assigns to names and marks.

luna: The section reads the ark's movement under God's name; this verse makes Noah and the ark a sign for الْعَالَمِينَ. | terra: Noah and the people of the ark are made a sign for the worlds. The surviving vessel and its people become a public trace through which a later world recognizes the event.

luna: The section's ruined town is read as a sign; this verse says a clear sign, آيَةً بَيِّنَةً, was left from the town of Lot. | terra: God says He left from the destroyed town a clear sign for people who understand. This makes the remaining ruin itself an intelligible mark rather than merely a past event.
terra: God creates the heavens and earth in truth, and this contains a sign for believers. The verse supplies the broad creation-to-sign relation underlying عالمين.
luna: The source-section explains ع ل م through a sign that enables knowing; this verse calls the revelation clear signs, آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ, in the breasts of those given عِلْم.

luna: The section presents creation's variety as identifying signs; this verse calls differences of tongues and colors among His signs, آيَاتِهِ. | terra: The diversity of languages and colors is among God's signs. Created differences themselves become distinguishing marks through which the plurality of the worlds is known.
luna: The source-section dictionary form وَسْم is a trace one reads; this verse tells the reader to look at آثار رحمة الله in the revived earth.
luna: The source-section distinguishes a true identifying name from an empty label; this verse says adopted sons are not actual sons despite people's words.

luna: The source-section says a name should identify its bearer; this verse commands calling adopted children by their fathers' names as more just with God. | terra: Calling adopted children by their fathers' names is declared more just before God. The verse makes the name a safeguard of true relation and recognition.
terra: Outer garments are prescribed so women may be recognized and not harmed. Dress becomes an outward, protective sign of identity, like the section's mark made for knowing.
luna: The source-section root س م و links the name to elevation; here the good word, الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ, ascends to God.
terra: Fruits, mountains, and paths appear in differing colors, including intensely black. The verse makes visible differentiation within creation into signs a reader can observe.
terra: People, animals, and livestock likewise differ in colors, and those with knowledge fear God. Species and visible distinctions meet the section's claim that each kind of creation is a sign.
luna: The section's world is a field of signs; this verse calls the revived dead earth a sign and points to grain growing from it.
luna: The section says creation can be read as a mark; this verse calls the night a sign when daylight is drawn away.
luna: The section places Noah's vessel under God's name; this verse calls the loaded ship itself a sign, آيَةً لَهُمْ.
luna: This continuation extends the ship sign in 36:41 to other vessels people ride, broadening the reader's view from Noah's ark to conveyances.

luna: The source-section describes good renown passing among people; Noah is left in later generations as a remembered name. | terra: God says He left Noah among later generations; the following greeting makes the lasting mention favorable. This supplies another Qur'anic form of the good name that survives among people.
luna: This neighbor completes Noah's preserved mention with the public greeting سَلَامٌ عَلَىٰ نُوحٍ فِي الْعَالَمِينَ.

luna: The section's good name spreads through generations; Abraham is left in later generations. | terra: God says He left Abraham among later generations; the next verse's greeting clarifies the enduring honorable remembrance, parallel to a lofty truthful mention.
luna: This neighbor supplies the public greeting سَلَامٌ عَلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ that completes Abraham's lasting mention.

luna: The section says a good mention continues among people; Moses and Aaron are left in later generations. | terra: God says He left Moses and Aaron among later generations. The line preserves their paired public remembrance after the rescue narrative.
luna: This neighbor supplies the public greeting سَلَامٌ عَلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ وَهَارُونَ, completing their continued mention.

luna: The section's good name is carried among people; Elijah is left in later generations. | terra: God says He left Elijah among later generations; the following greeting completes the image of a prophet's name remaining recognizable after him.
luna: This neighbor gives the public greeting سَلَامٌ عَلَىٰ إِلْ يَاسِينَ, completing Elijah's continued mention.

luna: The section contrasts Allah's known name with invented names; this verse says disbelievers recoil when Allah alone is mentioned but rejoice at other names. | terra: When Allah alone is mentioned, some hearts recoil, while mention of others pleases them. The verse exposes competing names as signals of allegiance rather than neutral labels.
luna: The section's burned mark makes the bearer readable; here hearing, sight, and skins testify to what people did.
luna: The source-section pictures a mark on skin; this continuation has the skins answer that Allah made them speak, exposing their owners' deeds.
luna: The section distinguishes a sign from what it identifies; sun, moon, night, and day are signs, yet the verse forbids worshipping them and directs worship to their Creator.
luna: The section treats created things as readable signs; this verse calls the revived, once-humbled earth one of God's signs.

luna: The section says the worlds are signs by which the Lord becomes known; this verse promises signs in the horizons and within people until the truth is clear. | terra: God promises to show signs on the horizons and in people themselves until truth becomes clear. It generalizes the section's readable mark from a brand to world and self.
terra: The creation of the heavens, earth, and the creatures dispersed through them are signs. This most directly matches the section's reading of the worlds and every created kind as markers.

luna: The source-section dictionary form أَعْلَام means standards or mountains; here sailing ships themselves are signs and rise like الأعلام. | terra: Ships move on the sea like الْأَعْلَام, towering visible markers; the section's banner word becomes a large, recognizable form on the water.
luna: The section names the ark's motion and stopping; after 42:32 calls sailing ships signs like standards, this verse says God's wind can hold them still.
luna: The source-section connects invoking God to the start of a journey; this verse tells riders to remember their Lord when settled on a conveyance.
luna: This neighbor gives the riding invocation, سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا, paralleling Noah's naming of the ark's motion.
luna: The source-section dictionary form أَثَر is a trace; this verse speaks of a people following their fathers' آثار, an indirect inherited-tradition parallel rather than a literal brand.

terra: The immediately preceding referent is called a عِلْم for the Hour, a knowledge-marker in the text. This lets the section's علم move from knowing an object to an event that signals what is coming.

luna: The section calls creation a collection of signs; this verse identifies signs in the heavens and earth for believers. | terra: The heavens and earth contain signs for believers; creation is presented as something whose visible order points beyond itself.

luna: The section says created kinds distinguish and reveal; the creation of humans and scattered animals is explicitly called signs for people of certainty. | terra: In human creation and the creatures God spreads are signs for people of certainty. The verse makes living kinds, central to the section's عالمين image, readable evidence.

luna: The section makes the created order readable; this verse names night and day, rain, and winds as signs for people who reason. | terra: The alternation of night and day, rain, revived earth, and turning winds are signs for people who reason; changing natural patterns are ordered markers rather than mute events.
luna: The section's root ع ل م links signs to knowing and mentions traces; this verse challenges claims for other gods with a demand for creation, authority, scripture, or أَثَارَةٍ مِنْ عِلْمٍ.
luna: The source-section treats an outward mark as identifying; this verse says the Prophet would recognize hypocrites by their سِيمَاهُم.

luna: The section's brand or sign identifies its bearer; this verse locates the believers' distinguishing mark on their faces, سِيمَاهُم. | terra: Their سِيمَا is in their faces from the trace of prostration; a bodily trace visibly identifies worship, joining the section's mark to worship under God's name.

luna: The source-section gloss says a good name spreads in goodness, not evil; this verse forbids insulting epithets and calls the post-faith name of wrongdoing an evil name, بِئْسَ الِاسْمُ الْفُسُوقُ.

luna: The section says created kinds are marks by which one knows them; peoples and tribes are made لِتَعَارَفُوا, so their distinctions serve recognition. | terra: Peoples and tribes are made so that people may know one another. Human differentiation has a stated recognitional purpose, a social parallel to the section's distinguishing sign.

luna: The section says creation is marked for recognition; this verse says there are signs on earth for those with certainty. | terra: In the earth are signs for those certain in faith. The ground beneath the reader becomes part of the world the section calls a field of signs.

luna: The source-section image extends signs to every created kind; this neighbor places signs within human selves as well. | terra: There are signs in yourselves as well; the verse turns the reader from external marks to the self as a recognizable sign.
terra: The angels' stones are مُسَوَّمَة for the excessive; this repeats the image of a mark that distinguishes and designates its object.
luna: The source section connects traces of a ruined town with discerning its lesson; this verse says a sign was left there for those who fear punishment.
luna: This verse supplies two concrete idol names, al-Lat and al-Uzza; the passage's later critique at 53:23 says such names were assigned by people without authority.
luna: This verse adds Manat to the named idols; the passage's critique at 53:23 supplies the point that these are human-given names without authority.

luna: The source-section says a name can be a sign with nothing true beneath it; this verse calls the idols names people and their fathers invented without God's authority. | terra: The alleged deities are only names named by people and their fathers, with no proof sent down. This repeats the boundary between a name that discloses and one that merely circulates.
terra: Those who reject the Hereafter give the angels female names. This is a concrete false naming that contrasts with a name grounded in what it truly makes known.
luna: This ayah supplies the ark antecedent for the section's later sign: Noah is carried in a vessel of planks and nails before 54:15 says it was left as a sign.
luna: This continuation says the ark sails under God's watch; 54:15 then names the surviving vessel as a sign, adding divine care to the marked scene.

luna: The section names Noah's vessel; after the flood this verse says the ship was left as آيَة, a surviving trace to remember. | terra: The verse says that the preceding vessel or event was left as a sign and asks who will remember. Its own contribution is the preservation of a trace for recognition across time.

luna: The source-section dictionary form أَعْلَام means standards; ships carried high on the sea are compared to them, making the raised-sign image visible. | terra: The ships raised on the sea are like الْأَعْلَام. Repeating the marker image makes their height and visibility part of what identifies them.

luna: The section's mark makes a person recognizable; this verse says criminals are known by their سِيمَاهُم. | terra: Criminals are recognized by their سِيمَا and seized; this is the adverse judicial counterpart to the section's claim that an imprint lets one be known.
luna: The section's image makes a mark identify its bearer; after 55:41 identifies criminals by their marks, this verse identifies the destination as Hell.

luna: The source-section treats اسم as a raised, honored identifier; this verse blesses the Lord's name and names His majesty and generosity. | terra: Blessed is the name of the Lord of majesty and generosity. The verse makes the name itself exalted, directly echoing the section's raised sign.

luna: The source-section connects the name to elevation; the command is to glorify باسم ربك العظيم, the name of the Lord the Great. | terra: Glorifying the name of the Great Lord makes the name the object of exaltation, parallel to 87:1's Most High Lord.

luna: The source-section links a name with honor; this repeated command again says to glorify باسم ربك العظيم. | terra: The closing command to glorify the name of the Great Lord repeats the elevated-name action after the surah's scenes of creation and judgment.
luna: The source-section's name marks the actual identity of its bearer; this verse says a wife called a man's mother is not truly his mother.
luna: The source section places the separate roots س م و (height) and ع ل م (knowing) together; this verse raises people given عِلْم in degrees, though عِلْم here means knowledge, not a sign.

luna: The source-section treats names as signs by which the named is known; this verse lists Allah's names as Creator, Fashioner, and the possessor of الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَىٰ. | terra: Allah is Creator, Originator, and Fashioner, and His are the most beautiful names; the names identify through the acts and qualities that make their bearer known.
terra: Jesus announces a later messenger whose name is Ahmad. The stated name is an identifying sign within the announcement, rather than an empty title.
luna: The source section's brand at 68:16 marks a rejecter; this immediate predecessor says he calls God's verses tales of the ancients, supplying the rejection the mark follows.

luna: The source-section dictionary form وَسْم is a brand; this verse threatens to place a visible brand, سَنَسِمُهُ, on a person's nose. | terra: The section's و س م is a brand that makes a creature known; God promises to brand the hostile denier on the snout, making the identifying mark punitive rather than honorific.

luna: The source-section's name-as-honored-sign meets the command to glorify باسم ربك العظيم. | terra: The surah closes by commanding glorification of the Great Lord's name, preserving the connection between the spoken name and divine greatness.

luna: The source-section links name, knowledge, and worship; this verse commands remembering the name of one's Lord and devoting oneself to Him. | terra: Remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself wholly to Him. The name leads into the patient worship that 19:65 also connects with knowing its unique bearer.

luna: The source-section treats the name as an invoked mark; this verse commands remembering the name of one's Lord morning and evening. | terra: Remember the name of your Lord morning and evening. The recurrent spoken name makes invocation a continuing orientation, not a one-time label.
luna: The section's mark makes a person recognizable; this verse presents radiant faces as a visible sign of their state.
luna: This continuation completes the radiant faces with their smiling and rejoicing, making their condition legible.
luna: This verse reverses the radiant-face scene with faces carrying dust, a visible mark of the other group.
luna: This continuation adds darkness covering the dusty faces, completing the contrary visible sign.
luna: This verse identifies the people bearing the dark facial signs as disbelievers and wicked, completing what the marks disclose.
luna: The source image is a mark by which a person is recognized; this verse says bliss is recognizable in their faces, نَضْرَةَ النَّعِيمِ.
luna: The verse calls the drink رَحِيقٍ مَخْتُومٍ, matching the section's brand as a mark; 83:26 says its seal/finish is musk, though خِتَام may refer to its final taste rather than a physical seal.

luna: The source-section root س م و means height and explains اسم as a raised identifier; this command joins اسم with الْأَعْلَى. | terra: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High. Name, Lord, and elevation are explicitly together, matching the section's derivation of ism from height.

luna: The source-section joins God's name with worship; this verse says the successful person remembers his Lord's name and prays. | terra: The successful person remembers the name of his Lord and prays; this pairs the name with the worship response developed beside 87:1 in the section.

luna: The source-section gloss says a good name spreads among people; this verse says, وَرَفَعْنَا لَكَ ذِكْرَكَ, your mention was raised. | terra: God says He raised Muhammad's mention. This is the section's good name spreading among people rendered as an explicitly elevated remembrance.

luna: The source-section says a name marks the beginning of an act; here reading begins بِاسْمِ the Lord who created. | terra: Read in the name of the Lord who created: reading itself begins under the name, and creation supplies the identifying act behind the Lord's designation.

luna: The source-section's reading begins by naming the Creator; this neighbor says the Lord taught by the pen, a tool that raises visible marks into knowledge. | terra: After the command to read in the Lord's name, God is described as teaching by the pen. Writing supplies a material practice through which names and distinguishing signs become knowable.

luna: This neighbor completes the pen image by saying God taught humanity what it did not know, linking a written sign to knowing. | terra: God teaches the human what he did not know. This completes the opening command to read in the Lord's name by making learning and recognition its stated divine gift.
luna: The source-section's name identifies its bearer; this verse begins قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ, naming Allah as the One.
luna: The source-section's سَمِيّ is an equal deserving the name; this verse denies that anyone is كُفُوًا, His counterpart.
